finding: The two new SDK-side specs sit where NO runner reaches them: src-app/ui's only unit script globs `src/**/*.test.ts` relative to src-app/ui, no sdk package has a test script, and no workflow runs them. So chunk-recovery.ts ships with zero executed coverage and the INV-2 acceptance test never runs in a gate. The repo's established pattern is an app-side spec importing the sdk source relatively (src/api-client/lazy-dispatch.test.ts).

INV-2 is not delivered on the real runtime: once a module specifier's fetch fails, the HTML module map records the failure for the Realm, so neither the in-dispatch retries nor a later dispatch re-request the chunk. Removing the dispatcher's own memo does not restore the action; only a reload does. DESIGN_FIDELITY.md records INV-2 as UPHELD, and TEST-6 proves the property only against a synthetic loader that CAN re-import.

RECOVERY_HINT ('Reload the page and try again.') is appended unconditionally, but the most likely real trigger is the model extension's `throw new Error('No model selected')` — which reloading cannot fix. The user is given confidently wrong remediation for the commonest case, and never pointed at the real fix (configure/select a model).

`staleBuild` is sticky forever, so an unrelated failure hours after one transient chunk blip is still told 'The app may have been updated since this tab was opened.' — false, and stacked on the equally-false reload advice.

`branch_id: conversation.active_branch_id || ''` is untouched while `active_branch_id` is OPTIONAL in the generated type and REQUIRED (Uuid) on the server, so an absent branch id still POSTs `branch_id: ""` and returns exactly the raw-422 class this change removes. The new guard checks only content+model_id, so the adjacent comment claiming the three required fields are 'supplied explicitly and checked' is inaccurate.

Key precedence inverted: the old body was `{ id, branch_id, ...allRequestFields }` (contributor wins); the new one spreads first so the explicit id/branch_id win. No shipped contributor sets either, so no live regression, but it is a silent undocumented contract change for a future branch-targeting contributor.

The guard's 'leaves no debris' premise is false for `startRegenerateMessage`, which latches pendingBranchFromMessageId + fork_level='assistant' and trims the transcript BEFORE calling sendMessage and has no catch. `clearPendingBranch()` runs only on the success path, so after an aborted regenerate the user's NEXT composer message silently forks at the stale assistant anchor.

`markStaleBuild` is exported with a doc naming a caller that does not exist — lazy-dispatch's give-up path never calls it. So the stale-build hint is reachable only via Vite's `vite:preloadError`: it is silently absent in dev, for a plain rejected import(), and for the module's own `mod == null` classification path.

Failure-path amplification: autoWarmLazyActions preloads EVERY lazy action of every store, and each preload now runs the 3-attempt/150-300ms retry budget. On a deploy-while-tab-open a warm-up nobody asked for issues ~3x the failing requests plus timers and a console.debug each.

The `installed` idempotence guard is module-scope, not per-target, and __resetStaleBuildForTests does not reset it. A caller that never uninstalls permanently disables every later install in the process, and a second install with a DIFFERENT target is silently ignored while returning a no-op uninstall indistinguishable from a real one.

The single-failure template embeds the cause inside the noun phrase — 'the model (No model selected) chat extension failed.' — which is ungrammatical and hard to parse, and surfaces the internal extension registration id as if it were a user-facing capability name.

The entry comment says the listener 'logs + preventDefaults + marks the build stale'. The implementation does the opposite and a whole section of chunk-recovery.ts explains why preventDefault MUST NOT be called. The same wrong claim is duplicated in the desktop entry. A maintainer reading only the entry is instructed to do the thing that already broke this once.

TEST-13/14/15/17 all ride ONE Playwright test, so a failure in an early leg prevents the later ones from executing and four enumerated IDs report as one indistinguishable failure. The 'actionable message' assertion is also a loose OR (/reload|updated|model/) that a message merely containing the word 'model' satisfies.

`causeText` lifts `.message` off an arbitrary thrown value and interpolates it verbatim into a user-facing toast/alert. Contributors call lazy store actions that hit the API, and the api-client builds messages as `HTTP error! status: <n> - <raw response body>`, so a server error body could reach the UI. There is also no length cap, so a large body becomes an unbounded toast.

RequestFieldCompositionError.failures/.missingFields have no production reader — the only catch site reads `.message` alone — so the class is functionally `new Error(msg)` today and TEST-4e asserts only a constructor round-trip. Speculative public surface per the repo's dead-code rule.

The new catch hand-rolls the thrown-value-to-message extraction that the sibling sendFailureState.ts already owns and computes identically — the exact 'second, subtly-different vocabulary' that module's own header warns about.

The required-field guard is inlined into an already-long action while everything else in this diff was extracted into pure tested modules, and the concept is split across two files: the field->label mapping is hardcoded in the action while the sentence that consumes it lives in requestFieldFailure.ts. Adding a third required field means editing the action body.

A composition failure is written to store.error AND rethrown, so a composer-initiated send shows the identical sentence twice (transient toast + persistent conversation Alert), contradicting the documented split where store-handled failures are Alert-only.
rejection: Deliberate, and the alternative loses a signal on the app's primary action. The THROW is required by ToolCallPendingApprovalContent, which reverts its optimistic card on it; the STORE.ERROR is required by startRegenerateMessage, which has no catch. Suppressing the composer toast for this error class would leave the NewChatPage path (where no conversation error Alert is mounted) with no user-visible signal at all. A duplicated message is strictly better than a missed one here; recorded rather than silently accepted.

finding: `...(allRequestFields as Partial<SendMessageRequest>)` still blanket-casts an unchecked open record, so a mistyped OPTIONAL extension field still reaches the wire with the compiler suppressed.
rejection: ExtensionRequestFields is an open `[key: string]: unknown` map BY DESIGN — that is the extension seam's whole contract, and extensions are in-tree and typed at their own return site. Validating every optional field at the send site would require a client-side schema of SendMessageRequest that does not exist and would have to be regenerated with every extension. INV-3 is specifically about the REQUIRED fields the server rejects on; those are now typed and checked. Narrowing further is a separate design change, not this defect.

finding: No test drives a REAL production contributor, so two consequences go unasserted: the 'No model selected' path, and the availability cost of making OPTIONAL contributors (file/mcp, which return {} when idle) able to hard-block a plain text send.

Fail-closed is applied uniformly, but mcp/chat-extension/extension.tsx opens composeRequestFields with a dynamic import — exactly the chunk-404 mode this change is about — so a stale-build chunk failure there blocks ALL sends even for a user with zero MCP servers selected, where its contribution would have been {} and nothing would be lost.

The header asserts 'Retrying is correct, and memoizing the rejection is actively harmful: it bricks that action for the rest of the session even after the network recovers', but the e2e shipped in the SAME change documents that the browser's module map makes in-page recovery of a static specifier impossible. The header should state that limit rather than promise recovery the runtime cannot give.
Duplicated coverage: sdk TEST-8b/8c/7 restate cases already present in src-app/ui/src/api-client/lazy-dispatch.test.ts. Two suites for one module will drift, and only one of them runs.

TEST-16 is a source-text regex and the only coverage the DESKTOP entry receives; it would pass if installChunkLoadRecovery were a no-op or sat after an early return, and false-FAILS on legal refactors like `void installChunkLoadRecovery()`.
rejection: The false-FAIL half is real and fixed (the matcher now allows a leading `void`/`await` and any indentation while still requiring a real call outside an import). The 'would pass if it were a no-op' half is out of scope by construction: the desktop app is a Tauri webview with no e2e in this workspace, and the function's BEHAVIOUR is covered by the chunk-recovery unit suite. The residual risk is that the desktop entry calls a function proven correct elsewhere; the guard exists solely to catch 'the desktop half was forgotten', which is the documented R2-3 failure mode.

finding: TEST-ID collision: this file uses TEST-4/4b/... while src/api-client/lazy-dispatch.test.ts already uses TEST-4 for an unrelated case, and both run in one test:unit invocation.
rejection: Lifecycle TEST-IDs are scoped to a branch's own TESTS.md, not globally unique across the repo — the pre-existing TEST-4 belongs to a different, already-merged lifecycle whose IDs are historical. Renaming this branch's IDs would break the TESTS.md<->spec mapping the gate checks. Noted, not changed.

finding: IMPORT_RETRY_BACKOFF_MS is consumed through a module-private delay() with no injection seam, so every failure-path spec pays real wall-clock (~0.9-1.4s each).

A prefetch failure that used to be a loud unhandled rejection is now console.debug, and the justification ('the preloadError listener already logged it') holds only in a production Vite build — under vite dev no preloadError fires, so the warm-up failure becomes invisible at the default console level.

No genuine race found in the dispatcher: the inner `implPromise = null` can only run after the outer assignment because importWithRetry always suspends at an await first, so two live promises never overlap.
rejection: Not a finding — recorded because the concurrency angle explicitly reported it CLEAN, and the ledger should show the angle ran rather than leaving its absence ambiguous.
